newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Rain, hail fall overnight.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Rain, hail fall overnight.

text.p: Rain and hail fell overnight across Kansas and Missouri, and grain dealers in the High Plains said Friday they were trying to determine if the hard red winter wheat crop had been damaged as a result.
One Kansas dealer said areas around Garden City, in the southwest part of the state, had received 1/2 inch of rain and "pea-sized" hail.
"I don't know if it did a whole lot of damage," the dealer said.
But one Oklahoma dealer said heavy rain and hail fell throughout his state.
"Enid (in north central Oklahoma) got an inch of rain, and western areas got as much as 1-3/4 inches," he said. "There are reports of hail in southwest Oklahoma -- golf-ball sized."
Meanwhile, basis bids for wheat were mostly unchanged and movement was light, dealers said.
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: K=KCBT May wheat futures. N=KCBT July. unq- unquoted, na - not applicable)
